subject: A microglial switch may separate who declines from who stays sharp
script: From Agewell Brief: A microglial switch may separate who declines from who stays sharp. New research pinpoints a shift in brain immune cells that may separate those who stay sharp from those who decline. Alzheimer's disease is often described by the buildup of sticky plaques and tangled proteins in the brain. But many people with these signs never develop dementia. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
